title: Give your coding agent one set of commands to check work
summary: A developer had AI agents set up and verify web apps with Vite+'s single set of commands. He reports CI dropped from 4 minutes to 50 seconds in one monorepo.
agent_role: The agent creates the project, writes code, runs the check, test and build commands, and fixes failures. The developer writes the instructions, reviews diffs and approves merges.
outcome: Author reports CI time falling from 4 minutes to 50 seconds and a pre-commit check from 11 seconds to under 2. He notes these are his projects, not a benchmark.
what_they_did: A developer used Vite+ on four projects for three weeks. It is a toolkit that puts building, testing and code checks behind one command. He gives the agent a set-up prompt and repo instructions. They tell it to run the check, test and build commands and fix what fails before reporting done.
how_it_went: He says the agent stopped guessing which command to run. Earlier messes like two formatters and three lockfiles stopped. He also reports much faster checks in CI.
worth_knowing: Moving an existing project over still needs a careful review of the changes. Also, the agent must not assume Vite+'s build command replaces a framework's own, such as Next.js.
prompt: Create a new [React + TypeScript] app in [folder] using Vite+. First read the current guide for Vite+'s create command. Do not overwrite existing files. Use one package manager and keep a single lockfile. Do not add another linter or formatter. After setup, run the install, check, test and build commands. Add a test for what you built. If a check fails, fix the cause and rerun it. Report the Vite+ version, the commands you ran and the actual results. Wait for my review before committing.

curation.rationale: A personal account across four projects with a shared setup prompt, repo instructions and timing numbers. It reads more as a toolchain review, and the 'define done' idea overlaps earlier entries.
